numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For the real-valued path, after the Amos Fortran->C translation, the output for `yv(300, 1)` incorrectly becomes `NaN`. It then fell back to cephes, which also incorrectly returned `NaN`. The complex-valued path for `yv(300, 1 + 0j)` also incorrectly returned `NaN` and had no fall back to cephes.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: In the original Fortran behavior (and prior to the translation), Amos correctly returned `-inf` for `yv(300, 1)` and `yv(300, 1 + 0j)`.
trigger_conditions: Use `scipy.special.amos.yv(300, 1)` (real-valued path) after the Amos Fortran->C translation
Use `scipy.special.amos.yv(300, 1 + 0j)` (complex-valued path) after the Amos Fortran->C translation
When Amos returns `NaN` for the real input, the code falls back to cephes for `yv(300, 1)`, but cephes also incorrectly returns `NaN`
oracle_clues: Prior to the Amos Fortran->C translation, Amos correctly returned `-inf` for `yv(300, 1)` and `yv(300, 1 + 0j)`.
After the translation, the real value path incorrectly returned `NaN` and then fallback to cephes also incorrectly returned `NaN`.
The complex valued path incorrectly returned `NaN` and had no fall back to cephes.

cephes `yn` termination condition was changed from `while (k < n);` to `while (k < n && isfinite(an));`, i.e., it now terminates when `an` becomes infinite/`-inf` to avoid further iterations producing `NaN`.

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: large n (test uses n=500) and x=1 (near asymptotic/negative asymptotic limit behavior)
category_specific_evidence: Regression test added: `observed = cephes.yn(500, 1); assert observed == -np.inf` (in `scipy/special/tests/test_basic.py`).
Asymptotic/termination condition bug: in `scipy/special/cephes/yn.c`, loop termination changed from `while (k < n);` to `while (k < n && isfinite(an));`.

PR description: missing loop termination when the intermediate answer becomes infinite causes further iterations to produce NaN; this ensures correct asymptotic behavior (cephes previously returned NaN; fix ensures termination when `an` is infinite).

PR/description notes: before Amos translation, Amos correctly returned `-inf` for `yv(300, 1)` and `yv(300, 1 + 0j)`, but after translation real path and complex path returned NaN; cephes also incorrectly returned NaN and fallback behavior was defeated until cephes was fixed.
reproduction_risks: Reproduction likely depends on using `cephes.yn` with real inputs matching the failing regime (`n=500`, `x=1`) rather than other values.

If you only test the higher-level `yv` paths, the evidence indicates multiple fallbacks and path differences between real and complex implementations; reproducing the bug may require exercising the `cephes.yn` code path where the loop termination was wrong.
Exact `-np.inf` comparison is sensitive to which implementation is called and whether the loop stops before producing NaN.
